yantra
(‘that which holds and protects’)
------------------------------------------
In Hindu ritualistic practices, yantras have an important place.
Originally, the word यन्त्र meant a machine or a contrivance. But in the tāntrik literature it assumed an entirely different connotation. It stood for a mystical diagram that would help the sādhaka or spiritual aspirant to control (yam = to control) his six passions and thus protect him (tra = to protect).
A यन्त्र is a geometrical diagram engraved on a plate of gold, silver or copper. It may be drawn on a bhūrja leaf (a kind of birch) also. It represents a deity. Different deities of the Hindu pantheon have different yantras.
A यन्त्र has to be consecrated first—this is called saṁskāra—with appropriate rites. It can then be used in worship. During the worship the यन्त्र can be used along with the image of the deity or a कलश (sacred water-pot) into which the deity has been invoked.
In tāntrik rites, the यन्त्र was used for षट्कर्मस् or six kinds of results viz., vaśīkaraṇa (controlling a person), stambhana (making one immobile), vidveṣaṇa (hating), उच्चाटन (expelling), māraṇa (killing) and śāntikapauṣṭika (for peace and nourishment).
A यन्त्र drawn on bits of paper or bhūrja leaves or even thin copper plates, and enclosed in metallic amulets, may be worn on the arm or round the neck for specific purposes. They are then called dhāraṇayantras. However one should be careful to see that they are not polluted by coming into contact with the earth or any defiling object like a dead body. They will then lose their power.
The following table gives a brief account of the yantras of some deities and their effects:
of Gaṇapati — for conferring wealth and prosperity.
of Bhadrakālī — for conferring know-ledge, strength, health.
of Sudarśana — for relieving sickness and driving away evil spirits.
of Śarabha — for curing epilepsy.
of Subrahmaṇya — for expelling evil spirits.
of Hanumān — for attaining strength, safety in travel.
of Cāmuṇḍā — to cause the death of enemies.

As regards the retention of the power induced in a यन्त्र, the following chart gives an idea:
Yantra inscribed on Duration
gold plate whole life
silver plate twenty years
bhūrja leaves twelve years
copper plate six years
